- When sentiment is positive (≥0.10) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10% below peak to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 1–2 days, adjust future forecasts downward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.05) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 3–5% to counteract pessimism.  
- If forecast mean is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply a 2–3% downward bias to future 30-day forecasts.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive values), reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome in early days of the horizon, apply a 5–10% downward correction to the first 7 days.
